name: Kalshi, Inc.
customer_base_segment: B2C US retail traders/bettors; B2B2C via Robinhood/Webull brokerage embeds
business_model_notes: CFTC-regulated exchange charging trading fees on YES/NO event contracts (sports, politics, economics, crypto, tech); peer-to-peer order book, not house-edge bookmaking.
revenue_traction: Sacra est. ~$3.5B annualized revenue Jun 2026 (up from ~$735M Dec 2025, third-party estimate); $52B cumulative event-contract volume by Mar 2026; $5.1B sports volume in one FIFA World Cup week.
existing_partnerships: Robinhood, Webull (distribution/embedded markets), xAI (Grok market-insight integration); investors Coatue, a16z, Sequoia, Morgan Stanley, ARK Invest
licensed_jurisdictions: CFTC-registered Designated Contract Market (DCM) — operates nationwide under federal law; sports contracts contested as illegal gambling by 20+ state regulators (e.g. Michigan restricted, NY federal suit ongoing)
responsible_gambling_stance: Criticized by state regulators (e.g. Kentucky cease-and-desist) for lacking problem-gambling safeguards required of licensed sportsbooks
foundation_model_approach: Integrates third-party models (xAI's Grok) for market insights; no proprietary foundation model
gen_ai_platform_partnerships: xAI/Grok market-insight integration shipped 2026; Google Veo 3 used for viral ad creative (marketing, not product AI)
proprietary_data_advantage: Real-time crowd-sourced event-probability pricing data across sports, politics, economics — a growing data moat

notes: Legal entity is Kalshi, Inc. (CFTC-registered exchange, trading as Kalshi). Founders Tarek Mansour & Luana Lopes Lara. Employee count conflicts across sources (150 vs 515) so left null rather than guessed. Most comparable to the Polymarket anchor (same sector); Kalshi differs by being CFTC-federally-registered (no crypto/offshore posture) which gives it a stronger nationwide-reach claim but also draws direct state-regulator legal attacks that Polymarket, as a historically crypto-native platform, faced less directly. Revenue figure is a third-party (Sacra) estimate, not company-disclosed — treat with caution.
